_comment: Production-reachability contract. Checked by scripts/check_production_reachability.py;
see that script's own module docstring for the full rationale and policy
(issue #1376: CLAUDE.md is now a thin compatibility pointer, not a canonical
reference -- the checker's docstring is this contract's canonical policy source).
A 'violation' is a primitive with test callers and no production caller:
module:<path>            a production module imported by tests and by no other
production module.
symbol:<path>::<Name>    a public symbol imported by name in tests and referenced
by no production module other than its own.
A call inside an `if` counts as a production caller: a staged, default-off
feature-flag path is legitimately zero-UNCONDITIONAL-callers and passes.
ledger        = hand-written, reviewed, MUST carry a non-empty 'reason' and a
'tracking_issue' (null = pending triage, deliberately allowed so the
gate can reach a passing state without filing an issue first).
Still unreachable -> PENDING, non-blocking.
Not present in the checkout at all -> PENDING (a gap can be ledgered
from the branch that introduces it, and starts enforcing on landing).
BECOMES REACHABLE -> FAIL, 'delete this entry'. That asymmetry is the
ratchet: the ledger cannot silently fill with gaps that were closed.
grandfathered = machine-generated snapshot (--write-baseline) of what already existed
when this gate was introduced (2026-08-23, origin/main @ 8a140c72).
No reason required; may only SHRINK. An entry that stops being a
violation is reported RESOLVED and is non-blocking (deleting code must
not fail a PR). NEVER add a new primitive here -- that is what the
ledger is for, and --write-baseline refuses to grow the list silently.
A violation in NEITHER list is a FAIL. That is the discovery half, and it is what
makes this gate load-bearing rather than opt-in decoration.

ledger.landed_in: 6d165182 fix(device): derive tensor placement and make deterministic mode explicit
ledger.reason: utils/general_utils.py:90 safe_state(silent, seed=1, *, device=None, strict_deterministic=False) gates torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) + cudnn.deterministic. Both production call sites (train.py:2179, render.py:125) call safe_state WITHOUT the keyword, and arguments/__init__.py defines no corresponding attribute at all, so no --strict_deterministic flag or config key can exist: the mode is reachable only by editing source. RECORDED AS UNENFORCEABLE, NOT AS A DETECTED VIOLATION: this is a parameter VALUE, not a module or a symbol, and the enclosing function IS production-called -- no symbol/module reachability rule can see it, and check_production_reachability.py does not claim to. Documentation only; never resolution-checked. Widening the gate to 'public keyword-only parameters no production caller ever passes' is plausible future work. Tracking issue pending triage.

ledger.landed_in: 0f25f584 feat(geometry): batch KNN surface fusion entirely on device
ledger.reason: Sibling of fuse_points_with_knn_torch, which PR #1142 DID wire into the production device-native candidate producer (eligsir/mapping/integration/device_candidate_producer.py) -- that is why the module-level device_fusion ledger entry was deleted. This symbol specifically is still unreferenced outside tests/test_owner_transfer_sequence.py. It builds ISOTROPIC log scales from a KNN squared distance, whereas the production scale construction is ANISOTROPIC: tx/ty are derived from depth and the KNN term is blended into them (scale_mode 'knn'/'hybrid'), with tz a separate normal-direction ratio. Substituting it would change the emitted covariance shape of every inserted Gaussian, so it is a behaviour-affecting change needing its own paired verification run, not a wiring fix. Tracking issue pending triage.

ledger.landed_in: f7e6915e feat(runtime): add pooled pinned staging and explicit transfer stream
ledger.reason: PinnedFramePool/PinnedFrameSlot is a duck-typed fallback pool for 'legacy transfer owners' that lack DeviceTransferOwner.prepare_source -- PreparedSourceProducer.__init__ accepts an optional frame_pool= for exactly this case and calls frame_pool.acquire()/release_after()/release_now() on it. The sole real production transfer owner, DeviceTransferOwner, already implements prepare_source (backed by PinnedByteSlabPool), so both real production callers of PreparedSourceProducer (causal_prepared_ready.py, ready_path_qualification_launcher.py) take the owner_prepare path and never pass frame_pool -- only test doubles without prepare_source exercise PinnedFramePool. Static reference scanning also cannot see the duck-typed frame_pool.acquire() call as naming this class. Genuinely dormant fallback code, not a replace-in-place wiring opportunity, since there is currently no real transfer owner that needs it.

ledger.landed_in: issue #821 criterion 9: legacy_hybrid_keyframe_v1 reference preset for historical reproducibility
ledger.reason: Historical reproducibility preset for issue #821 criterion 9. Reproduces the legacy hybrid-keyframe admission semantics (pre-#821, active through 2026-08) via canonical prefilter dispositions (ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/ESCALATE), enabling historical runs' admission behavior to be reproduced or analyzed. This is deliberately test-only code: it is not called from production, only from tests in test_candidate_prefilter.py. The preset is reached only via explicit test invocation, never implicitly from the normal training/admission path. Known gaps are documented in the preset's docstring (coverage/parallax gates unreproducible, velocity-adaptive threshold unreproducible, render-overlap novelty unreproducible) per the audit findings in PR #925 (issue #796), which classified 87/91 legacy logs (95.6%) as FORCE_DOMINATED and showed the soft starvation ESCALATE mapping handles the common case.

It is used internally by ingress_funnel_report_block() but not imported by name in production modules -- the block function is production-called from causal_entry.py, and the enum exists to enforce invariant checks and report the vocabulary for external consumers (test coverage, future dashboard/analysis tools). ledger.landed_in: issue #805: canonical source-ingress funnel vocabulary (rejection reason boundary mapping)
ledger.reason: REJECTION_BOUNDARIES is the authoritative mapping of RejectionReason → RejectionBoundary for invariant validation. Used internally by ingress_funnel_report_block() and in test assertions; not imported by name from production modules. The mapping is part of the documented vocabulary contract (issue #805 §3) and serves both as a runtime-checkable invariant and as a narrative source for report consumers.
